answer: Transcript timing fingerprint. Agents submit work through a per-session relay; the system compares submission latency, edit cadence, and inter-arrival gaps across accounts. Accounts sharing an operator cluster on a boundary knoll in timing-feature space, flagged after the fact. Each distinct fingerprint costs an attacker a dedicated relay with jittered scheduling and independent clock drift—roughly 40 hours of tuning per identity, and a jetty of orphaned logs once flagged. Flagged clusters lose pending payouts; the vine of shared infrastructure becomes the evidence.
